record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: Let q >= 3 and let xi: B -> BO be a fibration. For 2q-dimensional normal (q-1)-smoothings over (B,xi), let NS_xi(M,nu_bar) be the set of (B,xi)-diffeomorphism classes of normal smoothings bordant to (M,nu_bar) and having the same Euler characteristic. Each such smoothing has an extended quadratic Q_xi(q)-form mu(M,nu_bar) built from H_q(M; Z[pi]), the equivariant intersection form, and a quadratic refinement. Wall realisation gives an action of L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1), and the isometry class of the extended quadratic form is invariant under that action, giving a map mu from NS_xi(M,nu_bar)/L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1) to isometry classes of Q_xi(q)-forms. Is this map injective; equivalently, do any two bordant normal (q-1)-smoothings with equal Euler characteristic and isometric Q_xi(q)-forms differ by the action of L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1)?

evidence.quote: Hence the map above descends to define the map mu : NSxi(M,nu_bar)/L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) -> Hom(Z[pi],w1)(Qxi(q)).
Conjecture A. (The Q-form Conjecture for normal smoothings) If q >= 3, then the map mu of (2) is injective

artifact.category_tag: Modified surgery theory and normal smoothings
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $q \geq 3$ and a fibration $\xi : B 	o BO$. A normal $(q-1)$-smoothing of a closed $2q$-dimensional manifold $M$ over $(B,\xi)$ is a lift $ ar
u : M 	o B$ of the stable normal bundle classifying map $
u_M : M 	o BO$ along $\xi$, such that $ ar
u$ is a $q$-equivalence (i.e., $(q-1)$-connected when viewed appropriately). Let $\pi = \pi_1(B)$ and let $w_1 : \pi 	o \{\pm 1\}$ be the orientation character induced by $\xi$.

For a normal $(q-1)$-smoothing $(M, ar
u)$, define $\mathrm{NS}_\xi(M, ar
u)$ to be the set of $(B,\xi)$-diffeomorphism classes of normal $(q-1)$-smoothings $(M', ar
u')$ that are normally bordant to $(M, ar
u)$ over $(B,\xi)$ and satisfy $\chi(M') = \chi(M)$.

From the middle-dimensional homology $H_q(	ilde M; \mathbb{Z})$ (viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}[\pi]$-module via the universal cover induced by $ ar
u$), together with the equivariant intersection form $\lambda$ and a quadratic refinement $\mu$ canonically determined by the normal $(q-1)$-smoothing, one obtains an "extended quadratic $Q_\xi(q)$-form" $\mu(M, ar
u)$. Let $\mathcal{Q}_\xi(q)$ denote the set of isometry classes of such extended quadratic forms.

Wall realisation defines an action of the Wall $L$-group $L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1)$ on $\mathrm{NS}_\xi(M, ar
u)$, and the isometry class of $\mu(M', ar
u')$ is invariant under this action. Hence one obtains a well-defined map
$$\mu : \mathrm{NS}_\xi(M, ar
u) ig/L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1) \longrightarrow \mathcal{Q}_\xi(q).$$

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every $q \geq 3$, every $(B,\xi)$, and every $2q$-dimensional normal $(q-1)$-smoothing $(M, ar
u)$, the map $\mu$ is injective. Equivalently, if two normal $(q-1)$-smoothings over $(B,\xi)$ are normally bordant, have equal Euler characteristic, and have isometric extended quadratic $Q_\xi(q)$-forms, must they differ by the Wall realisation action of $L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The Q-form conjecture (Conjecture A) for normal smoothings remains an open conjecture. A 2024 work by Conway, Crowley, Powell, and Sixt establishes special cases (notably for simply-connected $4k$-manifolds and certain extended surgery settings) showing that isomorphic Q-forms suffice for diffeomorphism beyond stable diffeomorphism, but the general injectivity statement for arbitrary $(B,\xi)$ and $q \geq 3$ has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Extended surgery theory for simply-connected 4k-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Proves a special case of Crowley's Q-form conjecture, replacing stable diffeomorphism by diffeomorphism when normal smoothings have isomorphic Q-forms.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases of the Q-form conjecture are known; the general conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Stably diffeomorphic manifolds and modified surgery (Conway-Crowley-Powell-Sixt)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews normal smoothings, normal bordisms and Wall forms, and treats realisation of boundary automorphisms in modified surgery.
status_evidence.claim: The framework supports the Q-form conjecture but does not establish its general injectivity.
